turns.t: Right, so, I know I said on the phone it was just the tiredness, but honestly it's more than that now. I just feel flat all the time, and the baby's fine, she's gorgeous, that's what makes it so confusing.
Thank you for coming in and for saying it so plainly. So you feel flat most of the time, even though the baby is doing well. Let's take it one piece at a time.
Sorry, I'm all over the place. I haven't slept properly since, well, since she was born really, and she's five months now. Oh, and I forgot to say, my health visitor is the one who nudged me to come.
No need to apologise. The health visitor nudged you, and you're feeling flat. How long has it been going on, would you say?
The low mood, the low mood has been there about four months. It was worse in the first two months, then a bit better, then worse again when I started thinking about going back to work.
So about four months of low mood, in waves, with the worst patch at the beginning and another when work came into view. Is there a time of day it's heaviest?
Mornings, mostly. Although hang on, the evenings are bad as well when she won't settle. My husband says I'm being hard on myself, but he's lovely, he does the nappies.
Mornings, and evenings when she's unsettled. I'm going to ask a few straight questions, because I ask everybody who has been low. Have you had any thoughts of harming yourself?
No, no, nothing like that. I'd never.
Thank you for telling me. And any thoughts of harming the baby?
God, no. I'm terrified of anything happening to her, if anything I check on her too much. I got up four times last night just to see her chest moving.
That's very common, and I'm glad you said it out loud. What about panic attacks, those sudden waves of fear with a racing heart?
No panic attacks. I get a bit wound up in the supermarket, but nothing like that.
Okay. Now let me check what you're taking at the moment so I have it right. Last time we had you on sertraline, is that still going?

Yes, sertraline, 100 mg, one every morning with my tea. And the thyroid tablet, the levothyroxine, 75 micrograms, one a day before breakfast. Oh, and the iron, ferrous fumarate, one at night, the pharmacist suggested it.
So sertraline 100 milligrams every morning, levothyroxine 75 micrograms once a day, and iron at night. Is that the underactive thyroid you've had for a while?
Yes, the underactive thyroid, I was nineteen when they found it. And the anaemia, that was in the pregnancy, that's why the iron. I also get migraines now and then, but they've been quiet.
Underactive thyroid, anaemia, and migraines that have been quiet. Good. Has anyone in your family struggled with their mood?
My mum had depression, after I was born actually, nobody called it that back then. She told me last month, which was a surprise. Sorry, that's a tangent.
Not at all, that's useful. Your mum had depression, and it's something you've just learnt. Let me take your blood pressure and pulse while we talk, if you'd rest your arm on the desk.
Blood pressure is 112 over 70 and your pulse is 84 beats per minute. Both perfectly comfortable numbers.
That's good, I thought my heart would be racing, it feels like it is sometimes. Is it the thyroid, do you think? My sister-in-law said it could be the thyroid.
Your sister-in-law has a fair point. I can't rule out that your thyroid has drifted off again and is adding to the flatness and tiredness, so we shouldn't put it all down to mood.
So it might not be all in my head. That would be a relief, honestly.

It was never all in your head. Low mood after a baby is common and treatable, and the thyroid is worth checking either way. I'd like to repeat your thyroid blood test, and I'll arrange it for you to have today.
Brilliant. And the tablets, do I carry on with those?
Yes, we'll keep your tablets exactly as they are for now. The sertraline stays at 100 and we'll see what the blood test says before we change anything.
Okay. And the sleep? I'm lucky if I get two hours in a row. I'd like to sleep at some point before she goes to university.
Sleep matters hugely here. Could your husband do one night feed so you get a four-hour block? Even a few nights of that can lift things. Does that sound possible?
He did offer. I said no because he's got work, but I could say yes on the weekend at least.
Say yes on the weekend, then, and let the housework go. Please also ring us the same day if your mood drops sharply or those thoughts of harming yourself ever appear.
I will, I promise. I just want to feel like me again.
You will, and we're going to work on it together. I'd like to see you again in four weeks, once the results are back, and we'll go through them.
Four weeks, okay. I'll book at the desk on the way out.
Perfect. So, to say it back: blood test today, tablets unchanged, a weekend night off, and back with me in four weeks.
You didn't waffle, you told me exactly what I needed to know. Go and enjoy that gorgeous girl.
I will. Bye.
Goodbye, see you in four weeks.
